subtitle: Feel the moment. Feel your feelings. That's what matters most.

Disciplinary Action for Vice Admiral Ivan Ivanovich Burakov's Violation of Military Regulations (Draft)

    Ivan Ivanovich Burakov, holding the rank of Vice Admiral, currently serves as the commander of Zeno Arms Academy Cavalry Corps. He led forces in Operation Abadan, Operation Baikonur Cosmodrome, and others during the "Storm" war, earning numerous commendations for distinguished service. (Reply: Be clear on merits and demerits. List everything!)
    However, following the third "Storm," Vice Admiral Burakov deserted his post while on active duty and subsequently, on multiple occasions without authorization from superior command or consent from the individual, brought a human teacher Ms. Galina (Reply: Redact the name.) into Zeno Headquarters in Geneva. This conduct raised serious concerns among relevant human authorities, damaged the Cavalry Corps' reputation, and severely undermined peaceful relations between arcanists and humans. (Reply: Unnecessary.)
    Regarding Vice Admiral Ivan Ivanovich Burakov's unauthorized conduct in bringing a human into Zeno Arms Academy, following investigation by the oversight team and verification by the Military Discipline Department, the Zeno Arms Academy High Command has determined his actions constitute severe violations of the Latest Supplementary to Zeno Arms Academy Military Regulations (Draft).
    In light of Vice Admiral Burakov's repeated dereliction of duty and severe disruption of human life, having consecutively received three informal warnings, three formal warnings, and three severe warnings, Zeno High Command has decided to impose cumulative penalties sentence him to suspension without pay for twelve months. (Reply: Who authorized this? Are you desk officers going to command troops in the field?) The oversight team will dispatch personnel to supervise Vice Admiral Burakov's division to ensure compliance with this sentence. (Reply: Unnecessary. He follows orders.)
    Regarding Vice Admiral Burakov's violation of military regulations, all commanders and soldiers are urged to take this as a warning, strengthen their sense of duty, and strictly uphold Zeno military discipline.
    
Zeno Arms Academy Office

items.text: Dust Between Fingers
The militia camp is full of makeshift beds, sheltering the many civilians injured in the warlord's raid. The wails of pain echo in every corner.
Still, they've managed to set aside one private room.
Merel rises from her chair for the thirty-third time, pacing around the only bed in the room to check on the patient again.
The patient no longer oozes "death," yet she still can't bring herself to fully look at him.
Her gaze drifts aimlessly, toward the single basement window, the grain of the wooden chair.
A smudge of chocolate at the edge of the cloth catches her eye.
This Awakened has an unnaturally low body temperature, so low that even in Bereggrad's long autumn, a piece of chocolate wouldn't melt.
Could someone have used fire? Can fire even hurt Charon? Had her friend been turned over flames like a roast pig?

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Merel?
Merel feels guilty for the association, but in her franticness, her thoughts keep jumping around.
A shiver runs through her, as if her own hand had struck the match to the kindling.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Merel?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ah, oh!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Charon, you're awake!
She turns her face, quickly wiping away a tear, then hurries to Charon's side to help him sit up.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: H-How are you feeling? Are you thirsty? Are you in pain? I'll go get the painkillers.
Charon shakes his head slowly.
He has no need for water, and the medicine in the ampoule makes no difference to him. Besides, the body beneath his bandages has almost healed.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Oh, right, Marsha cut your cloak when she was patching you up. Here, I found a new one for you. Do you like it?
Merel is desperate to do something, anything, for him.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: That won't be needed, Merel.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: You owe nothing.
The cloth covering the "death" beneath shifts as if a breeze has just disturbed the air in the sealed room, muffling Charon's next words.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: No. I owe you a lot. What I did was wrong.
Her "no" is both a denial of him and herself.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'm an arcanist trained by the SPDM and the vigils. I even fought a little in Antarctica. I can fight, I can. But I didn't.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: We could've escaped together, if I hadn't run away.
A horrifying thought grips her.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I should never have forced you to take me with you in the first place.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: If I hadn't been so desperate to run off from the "XII," you'd still be tending flowers in the graveyard back in Montpaix, instead of ...

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: Death's call had grown heavy in the East. The path forward was clear.

items.speaker: Charon
items.text: So long as Krutov's atrocities grew unchecked. This was inevitable.
He tries to comfort her, but she is like a cracked cup, no longer able to contain her emotions.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I-I'll go get Andreas. I'm sure he's missed you a lot.
Perhaps escape is one way to heal wounds.
Charon doesn't stop her.
The streets of Bereggrad are barricaded with quilts, leftover firewood, and by the people who have refused to leave the city.
Women speak in low, anxious voices about what will come of this unusually warm autumn and about family who are now far away.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Hmm. I'm pretty sure the stable's around here.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Young lady. Young lady.
The tender sound of an old voice draws Merel's attention. She turns to find an elderly lady sitting in the shade beside the road.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Um, are you talking to me?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Yes, young lady. You were in Tamarovka, yes? Sergey said you were the "fish" he and his friends caught from the river.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Heh. If it weren't for them, I probably would've wound up in the stomach of some big fish.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Speaking of which, the soldiers have left already, right?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Ah, so you don't know either.
The lady's face falls.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: I saw you with those Foundation people. I thought you'd have some news from the inside.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: *sigh* Ivan sent his men to bring me to Bereggrad. He told me it would be safer there under the protection of the militia and the Foundation. He promised to take me to Zeno headquarters once he's back.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Ivan? Wait, you don't mean Ivan Ivanovich, do you? You're his mother?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: I am, dear. Though a child doesn't tell his mother everything, I'm sure he has his reasons. I've grown quite used to it.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: But, every time he suggests taking me to headquarters, I feel sad for the friends I made in the village and the red carnations in my little garden that soon they'll all vanish.
The old lady's sorrowful words make something inside Merel give way.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Young lady, tell me, are we heading into another era?
Merel nervously clutches the belt at her waist. She tilts her head, avoiding Ms. Galina's watery eyes.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I'm sorry. I don't know what you're talking about.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: No, no, I should apologize, young lady, not you. I shouldn't be saying such things.
The old lady gently takes Merel's shaking hands in her own.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: I'm just an old woman. Sometimes I don't even know what I'm saying myself.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Come now. Lift your chin and smile, young lady.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Do you think there's still meaning in this kind of life?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: It's like I'm trying to catch something, but no matter how hard I try to hold onto it, everything I do, every friendship I make, will just be blown away, like dust.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Well ...
Ms. Galina gives the kind of nod only someone with many years behind them can give and guides Merel to sit beside her.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: I was in a coffeehouse in Khreshchatyk, Kyiv, watching the Salyut 6 space station launch.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: There was a marching band outside rehearsing Праздничная увертюра—the Festive Overture. As the piece moved into the exposition, I saw Ivan push aside the drum major and run straight toward me.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: God! He barged into that coffeehouse so fast that he nearly shattered the door.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: And the first word from his mouth was "Mama!"
Ms. Galina breaks into a soft laugh.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So, did you believe him? That he was your son?
Her smile grows, and deeper lines appear at the corners of her eyes.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Did I believe him? I called the police three times.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: The first time, I told them I was being harassed. The second time, that he was a scammer.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What about the third time?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: The third time, I told them Ivan was a lunatic who claimed to be a time-traveler and should be committed to a sanitarium.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: But, every time, he was quickly bailed out by Zeno or the Foundation.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: He'd loiter around my building, holding a rusty tin box he claimed held "legacy items" I left behind. The nerve of that boy! I was still alive and well!

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: What was in it? Did you see?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Half a homemade cookie and a photo of the two of us. A photo so clear that it couldn't possibly have been produced in my time.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: He spent months following me to all sorts of places around Kyiv.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: One day, outside my building, he told me how I planted red carnations on the windowsill at his childhood home, but none ever bloomed.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: At the tailor's, he said that whenever a button fell off his clothes, he'd send it home for me to mend, and I would sew two buttons with irises on them.
She speaks slowly, the story she tells gradually becoming her own. Her eyes are filled with wordless emotion.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: I didn't share those memories, but over time, I grew attached to them all the same. Now, when I think of them, there's a bittersweet pricking in my bones.
She leans down, gathers a handful of dust from the ground, and lets it fall into Merel's open palm.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: You see, young lady. The wind does blow away the dust.
She helps Merel spread her fingers.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: But focus. Do you feel anything?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: I feel it slipping away, leaving me behind, as if it's destined to happen.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Exactly, you felt it.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: The excitement as the rocket soared into the sky, the surge of inspiration from the trumpet's cry in the Festive Overture, the heartbreaking ache in my chest as Ivan spoke to me of his mother ...

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: These fleeting moments ... I felt them and imprinted them deep into my heart.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: So then, the meaning of all this isn't in what we leave behind, but in what we feel as we go through it?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: A spark lives for its light and warmth, not for the ashes it will leave behind. Don't you agree?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: What's your name, child?

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Merel. Merel Van der Veer.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: My dear Merel, every one of us is destined to return to dust, so why not feel as deeply as we can while we have the chance? Feel every one of our memories, bitter and sweet.

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: Savor and cherish each sparkling moment, even if the "Storm" washes you away one day. Because, even if you no longer feel them, someone like my Ivan will.
She stands.

items.speaker: Merel
items.text: Where are you going?

items.speaker: Galina
items.text: To see what help I can offer, and to create more memories of this time before it's gone.
Merel watches her disappear behind a barricade. She moves with the strength of someone half her age.
And she looks down at the dust still trapped between her fingers.
